worlds.name: Hadley–Apennine
worlds.subtitle: Traverse the Apollo 15 landing region
worlds.credit: LRO / LROC NAC stereo • 5 m source cells
worlds.description: Survey mare and regolith terrain at the Apollo 15 landing region. Compare field measurements and bring both records back to the ship.

points.name: Mare reference station
points.observation: The Apollo 15 crew investigated mare basalt and sampled material near Hadley Rille. This station represents a game survey over the measured terrain.

points.name: Apennine transect
points.observation: Apollo 15 explored the boundary between dark mare plains and the Apennine highlands. The terrain grid records regional shape; this beacon represents a simulated traverse waypoint.

worlds.name: Jezero Crater
worlds.subtitle: Survey crater floor near Octavia E. Butler Landing
worlds.credit: NASA/JPL • MRO CTX / USGS stereo mosaic • 20 m source cells
worlds.description: Land near the Perseverance site and investigate Jezero’s crater floor. Braking, dust and the longer Earth link change the engineering choices.

points.name: Crater-floor station
points.observation: Perseverance studied crater-floor rocks near its landing site. Mastcam-Z and other instruments helped establish the volcanic history of this area. The beacon marks a simulated measurement station.

points.name: Jezero reference transect
points.observation: Evidence from Perseverance supports an ancient lake and river delta. This second waypoint records local slope and texture. The delta itself is beyond this walkable tile.
